title: Power Automate: AI-assisted UI automation repair in the desktop flow designer
summary: Hold: the table incorrectly says automation for the earlier runtime-repair control is undocumented; Microsoft publishes its writable Dataverse settings. The statement that Microsoft gives no initial state for shared Power Automate Copilot also overlooks the cited overview's on-by-default guidance.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: An eligible selector failure prompts the maker to capture the intended UI element.
claims.quote: When an eligible selector-related failure occurs, the system prompts you to capture the target element and its current selector.

claims.claim: The system proposes a replacement selector after the user captures the element for reference.
claims.quote: It then proposes a new selector in case an existing one does not work as expected, after the user captures the respective element for reference.

claims.claim: The designer option is named Run with AI-assisted UI Automation Repair.
claims.quote: In the flow designer, select the option Run with AI-assisted UI Automation Repair to start debugging the flow with the AI system's assistance.

claims.claim: Learn documents AI-assisted UI automation repair as a preview.
claims.quote:
AI-assisted UI automation repair (preview)
[This topic is prerelease documentation and is subject to change.]

claims.claim: The feature requires Power Automate for desktop version 2.70 or later.
claims.quote: You need version 2.70 or higher for Power Automate for desktop.

claims.claim: UI or web-page changes and broken selectors commonly require UI automation maintenance.
claims.quote:
Flows with UI and web automation actions often require maintenance when:
- Desktop applications or web pages change their UI structure.
- Existing selectors no longer uniquely identify the intended element.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The feature uses the failing selector and newly captured UI-element selector to generate a proposal.
claims.quote: the feature analyzes the failing selector together with a newly captured selector of the same UI element and proposes a more resilient selector

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Selector changes become permanently saved when the maker saves the flow.
claims.quote: The changes are permanently saved when you save the flow, as is the case with any other edits in the flow.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated an initial state for the shared Copilot in Power Automate setting.
claims.quote: If a region has GPUs (UK, Australia, US, India), Microsoft turns on Copilot by default.
claims.fix: Replace the final sentence of Why it matters with: 'The repair article does not specify the initial state of its required setting; the broader Copilot in Power Automate overview says Copilot is on by default, but describes tenant-level rather than environment-level controls.' Replace 'Microsoft documents no initial state for it' in the risk rationale with 'the repair article does not specify its initial state'. Keep defaultState unknown for the designer feature rather than inferring its arrival behaviour from the broader overview.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; rationale: risk; rationale: impact
claims.claim: AI-assisted UI automation repair runs only through the flow designer during debugging, rather than ordinary attended or unattended runtime.
claims.quote: AI-assisted UI automation repair is a debugging capability, available only through the flow designer. It doesn't automatically repair selectors during unattended or attended runtime execution.

claims.claim: Microsoft describes no new identity or permission model for this feature.
claims.quote: Searched: 'AI-assisted UI automation repair' 'permission' 'identity' 'settings'; 'AI-assisted UI automation repair' 'roles' 'permissions'. Opened the repair article and desktop Copilot prerequisites; neither specifies a new identity or permission model.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Applying a repair requires human approval rather than autonomous flow modification.
claims.quote:
Requires user review and approval before it applies selector changes.
Doesn't automatically modify flows without user interaction.

claims.claim: Skipping a suggestion without error handling stops the AI-assisted debug run.
claims.quote: If you skip the suggestion and no error handling is in place, the run throws an error and the AI-assisted debugging run stops.

claims.claim: Accepting a selector changes the affected action's behaviour.
claims.quote: If the maker accepts the suggested selector, it's added to the selectors list of the affected element, so that the action is updated accordingly and the flow can continue to run.

claims.quote: AI-assisted UI automation repair in Power Automate for desktop is currently available for organization premium accounts at no extra cost.

claims.claim: General-availability licensing and pricing for this repair feature are not yet published.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: AI-assisted repair requires the shared Copilot in Power Automate admin setting.
claims.quote: AI-assisted UI automation repair relies on generative AI models and requires the same Copilot prerequisite as other AI-powered capabilities in Power Automate

claims.claim: The arrival default of the designer repair feature itself is not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: 'AI-assisted UI automation repair' 'default' 'enabled' 'environment'. Opened repair article, Copilot hub and Copilot overview. Repair article gives a prerequisite, not its initial state; overview's generic on-by-default guidance does not establish this designer feature's arrival state.

claims.claim: The repair article gives Power Platform admin center > Copilot > Settings > Power Automate > Copilot in Power Automate > On.
claims.quote: In Power Platform admin center, go to Copilot > Settings. Under the Power Automate section, select Copilot in Power Automate, and then enable the On check box in the displayed pane.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls table and prose
claims.claim: An API equivalent for the environment's shared Copilot in Power Automate setting is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Copilot in Power Automate' setting API PowerShell pac admin environment; site:learn.microsoft.com/rest/api/power-platform 'Copilot' 'settings' 'Power Automate'. Opened pac admin, Dataverse organization Web API reference and tenant settings; no equivalent setting identified.

claims.claim: The runtime configuration is at Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Product > Features > Desktop flow repair at runtime configuration.
claims.quote:
select Manage. ... select Environments. ... select an environment. ... select Settings. ... Expand Product, and then select Features.
Desktop flow repair at runtime configuration (preview)

claims.claim: API automation for Desktop flow repair at runtime is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Writable columns/attributes ... LogicalName | isdesktopflowruntimerepairattendedenabled ... LogicalName | isdesktopflowruntimerepairunattendedenabled
claims.fix: Remove the Desktop flow repair at runtime row from controls and the rendered table rather than reporting its automation as undocumented. Microsoft documents writable organization columns isdesktopflowruntimerepairattendedenabled and isdesktopflowruntimerepairunattendedenabled at https://learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/developer/data-platform/reference/entities/organization#writable-columns-attributes; the organization Web API reference documents GET and PATCH at https://learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/developer/data-platform/webapi/reference/organization?view=dataverse-latest. The existing prose may continue distinguishing this earlier runtime capability from designer repair.

claims.claim: The preview runtime-repair configuration governs the earlier Repair with Copilot capability.
claims.quote: Find the Repair at runtime setting for the desired run mode (attended and unattended) under the Desktop flow repair at runtime configuration setting in the Power Platform admin center.

claims.where: controls[2].ui and controls[2].api; Governance controls table; Open questions
claims.claim: No dedicated admin UI or API switch specific to designer debug-run repair is documented beyond the shared Copilot prerequisite.
claims.quote: Searched: 'AI-assisted UI automation repair' 'dedicated' 'admin' 'setting'; 'AI-assisted UI automation repair' 'disable' 'Dataverse' 'API'. Opened repair article, governance, tenant settings and organization API reference; found shared prerequisite, not a dedicated designer-repair switch.

claims.claim: The Copilot hub documents environment-scoped settings.
claims.quote: You can configure settings at the environment level, with most settings also configurable through environment groups and rules.

claims.claim: A maker-group switch for this repair capability is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: 'AI-assisted UI automation repair' 'maker' 'group' 'switch'. Opened repair article and Copilot hub. Hub's user inclusion/exclusion control is expressly for model-driven apps, not this desktop repair capability; no maker-group switch found.

claims.claim: The desktop governance page directs administrators to contact Microsoft Support to disable all Copilot capabilities.
claims.quote: To prevent your users from using any copilot capability contact Microsoft Customer Support to disable all copilot functionality in your tenant.

claims.claim: The Copilot hub says most settings also support environment groups and rules.
claims.quote: You can configure settings at the environment level, with most settings also configurable through environment groups and rules.

claims.claim: The Power Automate Copilot overview instead describes tenant-level disabling and says environment-level support is unavailable.
claims.quote: an admin needs to contact support and they use a PowerShell script to turn it off only at tenant level. Environment level support isn't available.

claims.claim: Self-healing is a separately configured runtime capability.
claims.quote:
Enable self-healing per action:
Select a supported UI or browser automation action in the flow designer.
Open the Error handling settings.
Turn on Self-healing (Preview).

claims.claim: The Copilot overview ties Copilot availability in regions without GPUs to cross-geo data sharing.
claims.quote: If a region doesn't have GPUs (everywhere else except sovereign clouds), Microsoft turns on Copilot by default by toggling on the cross-geo data sharing.

claims.claim: The desktop Copilot page names a Copilot feedback tenant setting.
claims.quote: you can prevent users from sending Copilot feedback to Microsoft by using the "Copilot feedback" tenant setting.

claims.claim: The desktop governance page names disableSurveyFeedback for feedback control.
claims.quote: As a Power Platform admin you can prevent users from sending feedback to Microsoft by disabling the disableSurveyFeedback tenant setting.

claims.claim: Microsoft does not explicitly identify Copilot feedback and disableSurveyFeedback as the same setting.
claims.quote: Searched: 'disableSurveyFeedback' 'Copilot feedback'. Opened desktop Copilot, governance and tenant settings; read List tenant settings excerpt defining disableSurveyFeedback as NPS survey prompts. No explicit equivalence between the two names found.

claims.claim: The surrounding desktop Copilot preview documentation describes region and account-type limits.
claims.quote:
Create flows using Copilot (preview)
United States
Availability by account type
Currently, Copilot in Power Automate for desktop is only available for users with a work or school account.
